speaker: Marina
intro: Ahoy! Captain Marina Gale, island ferry. Last Tuesday my kitchen rolled more than my boat!
A captain who gets seasick on dry land? Now that's a case file.
Steady as a rock today, touch wood.
But my left ear's full of seawater, and it roars like the engine room. Some days it's nearly fine.
A full, roaring ear with good days and bad. Let's hear the whole story.

always_clues.text: Left ear: full, low roar, good days and bad days

options: Does your hearing change from day to day?
Yes! Some days the left is fine. Then a spell comes and it's underwater again.
Hearing comes and goes
fluctuating
Hearing that comes and goes. Remember that one!
Do you get seasick on boats?
Never! I once ate a fish pie in a force nine gale.
Any noise in the ear?
A low roar, like the engine room. It gets louder before a spell.
Low roar in the left ear, louder before a spell
roar
Any pain, drainage, dizziness, or sudden change?
No pain, no drips. But the room SPINS: two or three hours at a time, four times since spring.
Last one ten days ago. Good days since, and no new drop.
Room-spinning spells for hours
spinning
Have you had a cold or a blocked nose lately?
Not a sniffle all year. Sea air!
No cold or blocked nose
no_cold
Good: a cold can clog the middle ear and muffle hearing for a while.
What's the best sea shanty?
Anything with a chorus. Ten verses minimum.

joke_line: Shipshape answer, but not a clue. Ask about her ears!

red_flags.ask_line: Always check the red flags: pain, drainage, dizziness, sudden or fluctuating change, one ear only.
answer: No pain, no drips. But the room SPINS: two or three hours at a time, four times since spring.
Last one ten days ago. Good days since, and no new drop.
red_flags.card:
Dizziness: YES, spinning spells.
One ear only: YES = see a doctor.

extra_clues.text: Last spell 10 days ago; good days since

after_history: Oh! I brought my hearing test from my spring sea medical. It's on file.
Brilliant! Old results are gold. We'll compare them with today's.

otoscopy.caption: Marina's LEFT ear: an average-sized canal, shiny eardrum.
lines: Clear canals, healthy eardrums. No seawater, no barnacles.
Barnacles! You laugh, but I've seen things.

quiz.prompt: Her ear feels full. Is it fluid behind the eardrum?
options: No: type A, a normal peak. No fluid.
Yes: it's flat, type B.
Flat with a normal canal volume would point to fluid. Hers has a normal peak.
Yes: type C, negative pressure.
Her peaks sit near zero. A type C sits far to the left.

tymp.clue: Tymp: type A both ears (no fluid, no blockage)
after: No fluid behind that drum. The bone test will tell us where the fullness lives.

instructions: Tell her: press for every beep, even faint ones. Not for the roar!
Beeps yes, engine room no. Aye aye!
Tip: a steady beep hides in a steady roar. Keep it PULSED, or click the chip for WARBLE.

audiometry.intro: Better ear first, like the pros. I'll zip through the right!
Left ear's all yours. Keep an eye on the low pitches!
Right ear at Hoot speed: bone for her better cochlea.
before: Bone buzzer on her better ear first: the right. Unmasked bone answers for her better cochlea.

after_audiometry: Masked bone sits with the air: no gap. Not the middle ear.

reveal.title: LOW PITCHES DOWN
ask: Here's today's chart. What does her left ear show?
lines: Low pitches about 25 dB worse than spring, and she has good days: hearing that comes and goes.
Something like tides. An ear doctor can find out why.

evidence.prompt: What does Marina's left ear show?
options: Rising: worst in the LOW pitches.
A noise notch at 4k.
A ski slope: worst in the high pitches.
wrong: No dip at 4k: her high pitches are nearly fine.
Look left on the chart: the low pitches are the worst.
evidence.right: A low-pitch loss in one ear, worse than in spring.

findings.text: Low pitches 25 dB worse than in spring

lines.refer: Spins, a full roaring ear, hearing with tides: set course for the ear doctor!
lines.fit: Drop anchor! Dizziness is a red flag. Doctor first; hearing aids may help later, between spells.
lines.today: Her hearing dips with spells and comes back. No new drop that's stayed down. Soon, not today.

clue_pick.prompt: Present the evidence: why does Marina need a doctor first?
clue_pick.wrong_line: True, but that's not a red flag. What would worry a doctor?

wrong_lines.ear_clear: Those are normal: they don't send her to a doctor.
wrong_lines.tymp_a: Those are normal: they don't send her to a doctor.
wrong_lines.snhl: That's the type of loss. What's on the red-flag list?
wrong_lines.no_cold: No cold is good news. What's on the red-flag list?
wrong_lines.last_spell: That's why it's not TODAY. What sends her to a doctor at all?

clue_pick.right_line: Exactly! Dizziness and a one-sided, changing loss: a doctor looks first.

payoff: Today's chart and the spring one, side by side, sailing to the ear doctor.
I'll ask for an ear doctor appointment this week, not someday.
Hearing drops and doesn't come back? Doctor that day. Weakness, numbness, double vision or slurred speech? Emergency!
Aye. And then maybe something for the hearing?
Exactly. Hearing aids can help between spells, once the doctor has had a look.
Aye aye. My first mate takes the wheel till the doctor clears me.

headlines.S: CAPTAIN'S SPINNING SPELLS SPOTTED; OWL SALUTES SHARP TRAINEE
headlines.A: FERRY CAPTAIN STEERED TO EAR DOCTOR; LOW TIDE IN LEFT EAR
headlines.B: MARINA REFERRED; TRAINEE FINDS SEA LEGS
headlines.C: SOME BEEPS LOST AT SEA, CONFIRMS OWL
headlines.Do-over: MARINA BACK TOMORROW, FIRST MATE AT THE WHEEL; BRINGS FISH PIE

subheads.S: A rising loss, a spring comparison and a clean chart. The ferry runs on time.
subheads.A: Dizziness plus a one-sided, changing loss: a doctor looks first.
subheads.B: The rising pattern showed; a few stamps drifted.
subheads.C: Watch the low pitches, and compare with old results.
subheads.Do-over: Spinning plus one ear: always a doctor first.

fit.headline: TRAINEE NEARLY FITS A SPINNING CAPTAIN; OWL GRABS THE WHEEL
fit.subhead: Dizziness and a one-sided, changing loss: a doctor looks first.

today.headline: MARINA SEEN SAME DAY; DOCTOR: NO HARM CHECKING, BUT THIS WEEK WAS FINE
today.subhead: Her hearing dips with spells and returns: soon, not today.
